rows.derivation: Both spellings written in one DETAIL group: COLUMN 1 SOURCE K1 GROUP INDICATE, COLUMN 4 VALUE 'HDR' GROUP (INDICATE omitted; only GROUP is underlined), COLUMN 8 SOURCE V plain. Per GR1 the indicated items print only on the first GENERATE after INITIATE (a) or a control break (c): [AA HDR 1], [       2], (K1 AA->BB break) [BB HDR 3], [       4]. A parse-only implementation or one that ignored the bare GROUP spelling would print HDR on every line.

rows.derivation: Spellings written: 'ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL', 'ACCESS RANDOM', 'ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM', 'ACCESS IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS MODE DYNAMIC' (random_dynamic) and 'ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM'/'ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC' (sequential_default builders). defects.mechanism: GLOBAL on an elementary REDEFINES subject of the same shape: the contained program's bridge is emitted as 'ref __outer.WS_B' but the container has no WS_B member (the subject aliases WS_A's storage), and the contained body renders the reference as WS_A with no bridge -> Roslyn CS1061/CS0120. A group-subject REDEFINES works.
defects.rule_quote: If the GLOBAL clause is used in a data description entry that contains the REDEFINES clause, it is only the subject of that REDEFINES clause that possesses the global attribute.
defects.observed: error: backend compilation failed ... (65,48): error CS1061: '_PRG_L1C12C' does not contain a definition for 'WS_B' ... CS0120 ... '_PRG_L1C12C.WS_A' (exit 70; same at 2014 and 2023)
